claims.text: Rapid thermal annealing at approximately 1350°C for 5–10 minutes followed by rapid quenching will form finely dispersed nano-precipitates in a refractory high-entropy alloy.
The proposed rapid thermal annealing treatment will enhance high-temperature creep resistance.
The proposed rapid thermal annealing treatment will enhance high-temperature yield strength.
The proposed treatment will not increase alloy density.
The proposed treatment will not compromise room-temperature ductility.
Rapid thermal annealing followed by quenching will reduce internal residual stresses.
Short exposure at high temperature promotes fine precipitation.
Rapid quenching at a cooling rate above 200°C/min prevents significant precipitate coarsening.
The resulting refined precipitate microstructure improves creep resistance.
The resulting refined precipitate microstructure improves high-temperature yield strength.
The predicted mechanical improvements should hold between 800°C and 1200°C under sustained and cyclic loading.
Departures from the specified annealing temperature, duration, or quench rate may cause over-aging or insufficient nano-precipitate formation.
Over-aging or insufficient nano-precipitate formation would compromise the anticipated mechanical benefits.
